_units: robot base frame, mm, radians; rz = gripper yaw

plate._note: production plate measured with calipers 2026-10-19 (operator). Grip grooves are small: jaw width reads the same on the wall and in the groove (see gripper.readings). Height and groove position still to measure

plates._note: one entry per plate type (procedures/plates.py). grab_height_mm is added to every seat pose Z before a pick or place (vendor template VAR7). A type may carry its own jaw: {open: {short_edges, long_edges}, closed: {...}} in E1 pendant readings; without it the type uses gripper.open/closed, which the teach and measure commands write. id is SYSINVAR8 for the Lua path and lua/data_plate.lua must hold the same numbers. default names the type used when nothing selects one

gripper._note: open is per grip: the microscope holder limits how wide the fingers may be when descending

readings._note: value = finger gap. 2026-10-19 new fingers + production plate (small grooves): long edges 1.45, short edges 22.40, both measured in 0.1 mm steps with a clean stall. Fingers clamped on the wall ABOVE the groove read 22.37 (short) and 1.50 (long): 0.03 and 0.05 mm from the groove values, so the jaw width cannot tell groove from wall on either side; groove validation needs controller torque detection. Old teaching plate with old fingers read 2.84 / 24.0 (sd 0.001 / 0.007 over 985 grasps)

gripper._tolerances: grasp 0.08 (fresh grasp, measured sd 0.007); release 0.3 (0.6 mm, a carried plate may settle)
gripper._short_grip_2026_11_02: measured with tools/measure_short_grip.py: the jaw follows the command to 24.01 and meets the plate at 23.91 (refuses 23.75). The old closed width 24.83 (a hand reading) was 0.92 mm wider than the plate: nothing was clamped, every close read back its own command, empty or loaded. plate_width is what the pads read on the plate (what a grasp is judged against); closed is the command, 1.0 mm under it (the holding torque is capped, so the depth does not change the force); band = width -0.2/+0.5. An empty close reads 22.9, far outside.
gripper._long_grip_2026_11_02: measured with tools/measure_short_grip.py --grip long_edges on the plate on the module at 90: the jaw follows the command to 3.20 and meets the plate at 2.99 (refuses 2.70). The old closed width 3.71 (hand reading 3.68) was 0.7 mm wider: the plate was never clamped, it floated 0.35 mm per side in the claw, which with 1.4 mm to spare between the B-column posts gave the intermittent slide-in collisions. plate_width 3.0, command 2.1, band width -0.2/+0.5; an empty close reads 2.1.
gripper._clamp_2026_11_02: force close through the controller's Lua probe (devices/clamp.py): the jaw closes toward `closed` under a torque limit of 0.5 and stops at the plate; held = torque at the limit AND the jaw above the command AND near plate_width (0.7). Short edges measured: stops 24.03 at 0.5, -0.50 torque, unchanged after a 30 mm lift and 3 s. 0.5 is the highest limit the probe accepts.
gripper._plate_width_note: learned by the first holding force clamp of each grip (procedures/grasp.py _learn_width): where the pads stop on this plate under clamp_limit; closed = the clamp command, 1 mm under it; accept_band +-0.5. No grips step in the setup: delete plate_width (and the grip's closed) for a new plate or new fingers.
gripper._practice_plate_2026_11_09: ArUco practice plate, force close at limit 0.5 (runs/force_close_practice_*.json): on the plate the jaw stops at 22.38 (short) and 1.46 (long) with torque -0.50; empty it reaches the command (21.4, 0.5) with torque +0.56 and +0.36. closed = width - 1.0, band = +-0.5.

microscope._rule: inside the zone only vertical linear moves with fixed yaw; elbow swings happen below y 152 or on the taught route
microscope._needs_parked_note: the arm enters only while the microscope reports its stage parked (devices.squid parked); run.py homes the stage and waits for it inside the arm lock
microscope._free_above_z_note: From the operator (2026-10-28), heights above the base: stage lips 210 mm, stage 190 mm, flatfield module 260 mm; the platform top is robot z 35.6 (CAD 93 + k), so the highest part is about robot z 296. Above this height the no-swing rule (vertical moves only) does not apply, so the camera can be moved sideways to see the tag.

stage_sweep._note: the Squid stage's full travel envelope at its closest approach to the arm's origin: a y band ('a horizontal asymptote on y') no part of the arm, tool point, elbow or links, may cross at any time. Measure on the cell: {x: [..], y: [..]} in the robot frame, optionally z. null = inactive and preflight refuses

polar._name: rotation module: the plate turntable on the arm's base, driven as the arm's external axis E2. 'polar' is its name in the code

volumes._note: Solid things the planner routes around (routes/plan.py), from the manufacturer CAD (hardware.json 'cad'). Robot frame, mm. z is the CAD height plus k = -57.4, which assumes the wrist axis sits at the fingers' mid height; it is checked against the taught seats to about 1 mm (module top 59.6, hotel row-1 shelf top 66.6 against TCP 66.8 and 74.6) and is refined by one finger-on-platform touch (hardware.json cad.mapping.k).

limits._stage_park_timeout_note: how long run.py waits after home() for the stage to report parked before stopping; same bound as step_timeout_s, not a measurement

microscope._note: stage position (Squid stage frame, mm) where Microscope.home_xyz leaves it, and how far from it still counts as parked. Measure on the cell: home, read stage.get_pos(), repeat a few times. null = parked() refuses. base_path and experiment_id go here too (devices/squid.py)

_stress_profile_note: stress = 50/25/10 %, grasp tolerance 0.08 (10x the measured sd), slow zone 6 mm; validate supervised before unattended

lua._note: the program on the arm (setup/lua.py, lua/polar/mod_Polar.lua). profile: the speeds entry a job uses unless it names another; each of its fractions x100 is the controller's speed scale. zone_mm: blend radius between two straight legs of a stored route, -1 = stop at every point. v_linear and v_joint are the vendor program's own move speeds on this arm (VAR2 and VAR1 of its data.lua); jaw_v is the torque probe's default. NOT YET CALIBRATED against the PC-driven speeds: tools/test_lua.py speed measures it.
